A student cycles uphill from home to a shop, taking 10 minutes. The student then spends
5 minutes in the shop, before cycling home downhill at twice the initial speed.
Which graph could show the variation with time of the distance travelled by the cyclist?

hints: Notice the y-axis is distance travelled, not distance from home, so ask whether the graph can ever go down to zero after the cyclist starts moving.
Check the three time intervals in the text: 10 minutes cycling out, 5 minutes stopped in the shop, then cycling back at twice the speed.
Compare the gradients: on a distance-time graph gradient equals speed, so the downhill return at twice the speed must be steeper and take half the outward time.
walkthrough: Identify the quantity: distance travelled is the total path length, so it must stay the same or increase and can never decrease back to $0\text{ km}$.
First stage is 0 to 10 minutes cycling to the shop $1\text{ km}$ away, so the graph rises from 0 to $1\text{ km}$ with constant gradient over 10 minutes.
Second stage is 5 minutes in the shop from 10 to 15 minutes, so distance travelled stays at $1\text{ km}$ and the graph is horizontal.
Return speed is twice the outward speed for the same $1\text{ km}$ distance, so return time is half: $10/2 = 5$ minutes, from 15 to 20 minutes.
On a distance-travelled graph the return adds another $1\text{ km}$, rising from $1\text{ km}$ to $2\text{ km}$ with twice the gradient of the first slope.
Only the graph with rise to 10 minutes, flat to 15 minutes, then steeper rise to $2\text{ km}$ at 20 minutes fits. This is option D.

A.explanation: This falls back to zero and uses 5 minutes uphill and 10 minutes downhill, so it shows displacement from home with the wrong times.

B.explanation: This falls back to zero, so it is a displacement from home graph, not a distance-travelled graph which can never decrease.

C.explanation: This keeps increasing but the final section is less steep than the first, so it shows a slower return speed, not twice the uphill speed.

D.explanation: This never decreases to reach $2\text{ km}$ total, has a 10 minute first section and 5 minute flat section, then a steeper 5 minute return at twice the speed.
